title: Organising Your Brand Files: A Simple Folder System Your Team, Printer and Developer Can Use

cards.heading: Keep only approved files
cards.text: If it is final and a supplier might need it again, it belongs in the brand folder.

cards.heading: Use six clear folders
cards.text: Guidelines, logos, colours and fonts, templates, images and an archive for old versions.

cards.heading: Name files so they explain themselves
cards.text: Say what the file is. Avoid words like "final" and "latest", and skip spaces.

cards.heading: Send suppliers only what they need
cards.text: A printer, a developer and a new team member each need different files.

cards.heading: Record font licences
cards.text: Note where fonts came from and what the licence allows. If unsure, check the terms.

facebook.message:
Can you put your hand on the right logo file in under a minute?
If your brand files are scattered across inboxes and laptops, small inconsistencies creep in. Our latest guide shows a simple folder system that a printer, web developer or new team member can use without asking you for help.
Swipe through for the key points, including what to keep, how to name files and who needs what.

To read the full article, visit the FinTaxTech website and find "Organising Your Brand Files: A Simple Folder System Your Team, Printer and Developer Can Use" in our Blog section.
